record_type: Published to main on 2026-11-22 after owner approval in chat ('release as soon we're finished, no need to delay').
why: Second batch of damage and hardware-diagnosis guides. HONEST LIMIT: unlike the Nov 21 batch, these topics were NOT chosen from query or volume data. The Nov 15 Search Console export's unused evidence was exhausted and no keyword-volume tool was available, so each topic was chosen by analogy to a page that already earns impressions, then checked for overlap, source readability and whether the shop does the work.

not_built.xbox controller drift / not connecting: Xbox Support is a JavaScript shell needing about five more Microsoft hosts to read; owner says controllers are not his area
not_built.macbook swollen battery: laptop-battery-dying already covers trackpad and case signs
not_built.four more topics to reach ten: waiting on fresh per-page Search Console query exports or keyword volumes

rules: Every manufacturer fact from a page read on 2026-11-22; phrased 'Samsung says', 'Apple says'.
Owner house facts from 2026-11-21 applied (connectors rarely pop loose; a dead part is usually the part itself; no claims about speed of damage; tape cracked camera glass).
No invented bench stories, statistics or prices. Remaining questions are <!-- bench-note --> comments.
Mail-in stays 'Statewide' (Idaho). Bent devices: text photos first, no blanket mail-in offer.

guides.topic: Samsung 'Moisture detected' / water-drop icon, including on a dry phone
guides.owner_input: Owner has not seen the stuck warning often enough to say what it usually is: no bench claim on the page. USB-cache steps rest on Samsung's UK page (no US version found). Open question: does he clean or replace Galaxy charging ports.

guides.topic: Cracked iPad: safe to use, glass or display, glass-only versus full assembly by model
guides.chosen_by_analogy_to: cracked-screen-safe-to-use (27,337 impressions); iPad pages already earn impressions
sources: Apple tech-spec pages listing 'Fully laminated' for iPad mini 5/6/A17 Pro, iPad Air 2 through M3, iPad Pro 11-inch 4th gen and M4 models; not listed for iPad 9th, 10th, A16
guides.owner_input: Owner supplied the model list (tables in chat, 2026-11-22): glass-only on every standard iPad through iPad 11 (A16), mini 1-3, Air 1; full assembly on mini 4+, Air 2+, every Pro. Apple's spec pages agree where they overlap. CONFIRMED by the owner on 2026-11-22 ('yes glass/digitizer generally fixes dead touch zones'): page says a dead touch zone on a glass-only model is fixed by the glass/digitizer replacement (touch layer is part of that glass), and that lines or dark patches mean the LCD too. The model table is labelled 'By model' (not 'from the bench'): the owner supplied it as reference tables, and five rows were verified against Apple's spec pages by the integrating session.

guides.topic: Cracked back glass on a Galaxy or Pixel
guides.owner_input: Owner confirmed he replaces cracked back glass on Samsung and Pixel phones. Open: is camera lens glass part of the back panel he fits; which models he doesn't take; what he says about water resistance after the repair.

guides.topic: Power, volume or mute button stuck or dead after a drop; on-screen stand-ins
guides.owner_input: Owner: fairly uncommon in his experience; when it happens the mechanism is often physically bent or disfigured. Open: does a phone with a dead power button start when plugged in; what a stuck power button does on phones he sees.

guides.topic: Bent phone or iPad: bend versus bulge, battery hazard, don't bend it back
guides.owner_input: Owner: does not straighten bent frames; takes bent-frame jobs by replacing the frame and damaged internals; bent devices can be battery hazards. Open: which devices he takes; what he finds inside; whether he'll open one just for data.

guides.topic: Dropped hard drive that clicks, beeps or won't spin: stop powering it
guides.chosen_by_analogy_to: external-drive-not-showing-up-mac; data-recovery service page ranks for local data recovery terms
sources: Seagate Recovery Services data-loss FAQ PDF (2012, UK edition)
guides.owner_input: Owner: can often save data from drives beginning to fail but still partly working, and drives with damaged ports or other PCB issues; drives with damaged internal mechanisms or badly damaged file systems generally go to a data-recovery expert. CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: data-recovery.html lists clicking drives as Tier 2 in-house work (2-7 days), says 'data stays local' and 'no recovery, no fee'. Not edited; owner to decide.
